newsitem.title: CHINA: Migrant workers bring disease to Shanghai.
newsitem.headline: Migrant workers bring disease to Shanghai.

text.p: Shanghai's three million migrant workers pose a serious health risk, bringing back diseases that the city had wiped out, the Business News reported on Sunday.

Official surveys showed that, because of the migrant workers, the level of infectious diseases such as hepatitis, diarrhoea and typhoid had risen every year in the city for the last three years, it said.

The migrant workers also have brought back three diseases that the city had eliminated -- snail fever, filariasis and malaria, it said. Filariasis is a disease caused by a parasitic worm in the lymph vessels.
Some migrants have also brought with them tuberculosis, HIV and venereal diseases, the newspaper said.
The migrants, from poorer areas of inland China, mainly work on building sites or public-works projects and live in overcrowded and unsanitary accomodations.

The newspaper said that the living and working conditions of the migrants helped spread diseases and that they had inadequate access to medical facilities. They have a poor awareness of hygiene and the need for preventive medicine, it said.
It called for urgent steps to be taken to improve the migrants' facilities and health knowledge, especially to thwart infectious diseases.
Shanghai has a resident population of 13 million.
